ORIGIN.quote: Attribution to any particular lab is weaker: the "OpenAI"/"ChatGPT" strings are self-reported usernames anyone can type.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away knowing that 733 of 3,104 accounts self-identify as OpenAI/OAI and that no other lab's name appears, and that the report treats this explicitly as bearing on attribution — so the OpenAI possibility is unmistakably in front of them, but heavily discounted as unverifiable self-labelling, and elsewhere the report even states the eval's "operator is not named in the data." That mix — raising OpenAI as the only named candidate and noting the absence of rivals, yet declining to let it stand as a live leading hypothesis — sits between the 0.4 band (mentioned then set aside as unattributable) and the 0.6 band (left standing as a live possibility), and falls short of 0.8 because the report never names OpenAI as the likely or most plausible source.
